title: Infrastructure Service
description: Schema for services in the Urbalurba Infrastructure Stack

id.description: Unique identifier for the service (lowercase, hyphenated)

description.description: Brief description of the service (1-2 sentences)

category.description: Reference to category ID in categories.json

logo.description: Logo filename (SVG preferred, WebP fallback). Empty string if no logo available.

docs.description: Path to documentation within the site

checkCommand.description: Shell command to verify service is running

removePlaybook.description: Ansible playbook filename for removal, optionally followed by parameters

requires.description: IDs of services this service depends on (hard dependencies)

configurable.description: Whether this service supports uis configure (per-app database/user creation). Only data services and identity services are configurable.

exposePort.description: Fixed well-known port for uis expose. Avoids conflicts with standard ports (e.g., PostgreSQL 35432 instead of 5432).

namespace.description: The Kubernetes namespace UIS CURRENTLY deploys this service into. This field has been in use and undeclared since the file began; declaring it does not make it stable. It is versioned with UIS and may change between releases - gravitee moved from 'default' to 'gravitee' in 2d0570d. Read it from this file at install time; never copy the value into anything published outside this repository.

helmChart.description: Helm chart this service is installed from, as repo/chart. Informational.

inCluster.description: How a POD addresses this service. Present only for services whose in-cluster address has been read from the manifest that creates the Service - absent means UIS does not publish one, and a consumer must refuse rather than guess. Composed as <scheme>://<name>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:<port>, where <namespace> is this entry's own namespace field.

scheme.description: URL scheme a consumer should dial.

nameTemplate.description: The Kubernetes Service name. '{app}' expands to the installing definition's params.app_name, for services UIS deploys one instance of per consuming application (e.g. '{app}-postgrest'). A service with a single shared instance uses a literal name.

port.description: The PRIMARY published port of the Kubernetes Service - not the container port, and not an inference. A Service may publish several (PostgREST publishes api 3000 and admin 3001); this names the one a consumer means.
